privacy.title: Privacy Policy and Cookie Policy
privacy.intro: This policy describes how the personal data of users visiting this website is collected, used, and protected, in compliance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR - EU Regulation 2016/679).
privacy.section1_text:
The Data Controller is Stefano Videsott.
Contact email: stefano.videsott.work@gmail.com
privacy.section2_li1: Data provided voluntarily (Contact Form): When you fill out the contact form, we collect your Name and Email address. This data is used exclusively to respond to your contact request. The legal basis is your explicit consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR), given by checking the consent box before submitting the form. You may withdraw your consent at any time by contacting the Data Controller; this will not affect the lawfulness of any processing carried out before withdrawal.
privacy.section2_li2: Navigation data and Security: During navigation, the computer systems responsible for operating the site acquire certain data (e.g., anonymized IP addresses, user agents) whose transmission is implicit in the use of Internet protocols. This data serves solely to ensure site security and block cyber attacks or bots.
privacy.section3_intro: This site is built to maximize user privacy and does not use advertising profiling services. However, it relies on essential technical services:
privacy.section3_li1: Cloudflare: Used as a Content Delivery Network (CDN) to speed up the site and protect it from DDoS attacks. Cloudflare processes traffic data in an aggregated form.
privacy.section3_li2: Cloudflare Turnstile: An anti-spam verification system integrated into the contact form. It verifies that the user is human without using tracking cookies.
privacy.section3_li3: Cloudflare Web Analytics: A natively cookie-less and anonymized visit measurement system, which does not track the user across different websites.
privacy.section3_li4: Sentry: Platform for monitoring server technical errors. It collects technical diagnostic data (error logs, stack traces, and basic request metadata such as IP addresses and user agents) in the event of a site error to allow for its correction.
privacy.section3_li5: Umami Analytics: We use a self-hosted instance of Umami (at umami.stefanovidesott.com) to analyze website traffic. Umami is a privacy-focused open-source solution: it does not use cookies, does not collect personal data (IP addresses are cryptographically anonymized), and statistical data remains the exclusive property of the Data Controller, without being shared with third parties.
privacy.section4_text:
This site does not use profiling or marketing cookies. We do not use tools like Google Analytics or Meta Pixel.

The only cookies present are Strictly Necessary Technical Cookies related to accessing the site's Administration area (Session Cookie). Since these cookies are essential for the technical functioning of the infrastructure and do not track users for commercial purposes, current legislation does not require displaying a prior consent banner.
privacy.section5_text: Emails received via the contact form are kept in the Data Controller's email inbox for the time strictly necessary to process the request. They are not added to any newsletter or marketing database without explicit consent.
privacy.section6_text: Under Articles 15 and following of the GDPR, you have the right to request access to your personal data at any time, its rectification, deletion, restriction of processing, and — where consent is the legal basis — its portability and withdrawal of consent. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with the competent supervisory authority: in Italy, the Garante per la protezione dei dati personali (www.garanteprivacy.it). To exercise your rights directly with the Data Controller, send an email to stefano.videsott.work@gmail.com.

I previously worked as a developer at Airpim SRL and currently take on freelance projects for clients in Trento and across Trentino. I'm passionate about software development broadly — from backend systems to web applications — and I'm always looking for new challenges in the IT world.
home.about-desc-2: I have a solid foundation in Python, C++, C# and Java, and I'm comfortable across the full stack. I enjoy building applications that solve real problems, with an eye for clean and maintainable code. Whether it's a web app, a local-business site, or the occasional game.
home.about-desc-3: When I'm not coding, I enjoy playing music, exploring projects, experimenting with the latest in AI, and expanding my knowledge through blogs and tutorials.

portfolio.title: Personal Portfolio & Headless CMS
portfolio.subtitle: A full-stack personal project built from scratch
portfolio.what-is-text: A dynamic, bilingual portfolio website built entirely from scratch with FastAPI and Vanilla JS, paired with a custom headless CMS powered by SQLite. Every section you see on this site — projects, experiences, skills — is managed through the admin panel without touching the code.
portfolio.problem-text: Most portfolio generators are either too rigid (static) or bloated with dependencies. The goal was to build something fully dynamic, multilingual, and self-hosted, with zero reliance on third-party CMS services, while keeping the codebase clean and maintainable.
portfolio.tech-back: Backend: Python 3.14, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy 2.0, Alembic (migrations), SQLite.
portfolio.tech-front: Frontend: Vanilla JS (no framework), Jinja2 SSR templates, CSS custom properties for theming.
portfolio.tech-devops: DevOps: Docker, Docker Compose, Nginx, GitHub Actions CI/CD, Cloudflare CDN.
portfolio.tech-security: Security: Per-request CSP nonces, CSRF tokens, magic-bytes file validation, Cloudflare Turnstile, Sentry monitoring.
portfolio.feature-1: Full CRUD CMS: Create, edit, and delete any content section from the admin panel.
portfolio.feature-2: Bilingual (IT/EN): All content is stored in both languages; the UI adapts to the user's locale.
portfolio.feature-3: Dark/Light theme: Persisted in localStorage, applied before CSS renders to avoid FOUC.
portfolio.feature-4: CV Management: Upload and replace CVs (IT/EN) directly from the admin panel.
portfolio.feature-5: CI/CD Pipeline: GitHub Actions builds and deploys the Docker image on every push to main.

wannawork.title: WannaWork - Job Matching
wannawork.subtitle: Software Engineering Project at the University of Trento
wannawork.what-is-text: WannaWork is a Single Page Application designed to facilitate local job matching. It connects students, who can create profiles, upload resumes, and search for part-time jobs, with local employers, who can post jobs and manage applications.
wannawork.problem-text: It was created to solve the difficulty students face in finding flexible part-time jobs and to digitize local job hunting, which often still relies on paper resumes. By centralizing this process, it creates a direct bridge between small businesses and local youth, boosting the economy and youth employment.
wannawork.tech-front: Frontend: Vue.js 3 (Composition API), Pinia, Vue Router, TailwindCSS, and DaisyUI.
wannawork.tech-back: Backend: Node.js, Express.js (RESTful APIs), JWT for stateless authentication, bcryptjs.
wannawork.tech-devops: Testing & DevOps: Jest, Supertest, OpenAPI (Swagger), Docker, Nginx, Let's Encrypt. Dual deployment (Render.com and Self-Hosted on Arch Linux).
wannawork.docs-d1: D1 - Requirements Analysis: Pitch, functional/non-functional requirements, Use Cases, User Stories, and mockups.
wannawork.docs-d2: D2 - Design & Implementation: Architecture, RESTful APIs, E-R schema, testing, and deployment.
wannawork.docs-d3: D3 - Analysis & Design: Advanced UML Diagrams (Component and Class diagrams).
wannawork.docs-d4: D4 - Self-Evaluation: Critical analysis and conclusions.
wannawork.docs-bp: Business Plan: 5-year financial projections, cost and revenue analysis.
wannawork.role-text: This was a group project. I actively contributed to the initial analysis phase (D1) and was entirely responsible for drafting the design document (D2), developing the complete codebase (Frontend and Backend), and writing the final self-evaluation (D4). The D3 document and the Business Plan were handled by other team members and are included here only for project completeness.
